newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on funds, Brazil talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on funds, Brazil talk.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended firmer with soymeal near limit gains on aggressive fund and commercial buying and rumors Brazil planned to impose an export tax on soy products, traders said.
"We had a positive spin on the meal from the Brazil tax story," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "There just aren't any (sell) orders here."
Brazilian crushers and the Brazil Agricultural Ministry said a three percent export tax on soy products was unlikely and would be rejected by the ministry if proposed.

Brazilian crushers, whose profits have been cut since a previous tax was abolished last year, would benefit because a tax would discourage exports and make domestic soybeans cheaper and more available.
CBOT traders said a tax would raise the price of Brazilian exports and encourage world buyers to buy U.S. supplies.
Soymeal futures closed $9.70 to $2.00 per ton higher with May up $8.70 at $274.70. Soyoil ended 0.25 cent per lb higher to 0.02 lower with May up 0.11 at 25.38.
News two Cargill Inc processing plants at Kansas City and at Norfolk, Va. planned to take downtime also supported futures.
Traders said expensive soybeans and dwindling crush margins led to the temporary shutdowns.
Weekly crush figures were expected to fall as a result.

Gains were capped in new crop months by ideas 1997 soybean acreage would grow. Private analytical firm Sparks Companies reportedly pegged soybean acreage at 65.98 million acres, above USDA's outlook conference estimate of 65.3 million.
Commercials were conspicuous buyers of both meal and oil on the day.

Cargill Inc bought 200 lots May soymeal, 100 lots July and 500 December while Continental Grain bought 400 May, traders said. Cargill also bought 400 lots July soyoil and 200 lots May while Central Soya bought 200 lots May.

Funds were also aggressive buyers with Cargill Investor Services a buyer of 300 lots May soymeal and 500 lots December. Smith Barney and Tenco each bought 400 May and Refco Inc bought 200 May and 300 July.
Refco Inc bought 300 lots May soyoil, Smith Barney bought 200 May and Griffin Trading bought 500 May, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, against Thursday's actual volume of 26,285 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 26,000 lots, compared with Thursday's 25,071 lots.
